purpose: Canonical naming-style policy for individual Uma Musume skill names in Vietnamese. Follow the compact title rhythm of the zh-CN source while preserving Japanese meaning, motifs, proper nouns, symbols, and gameplay identity.
precedence: Exact source match in canonical_examples below overrides an older conflicting skill-name target from term_registry.json.
For other individual skill names, verified newer canonical registry mapping wins.
Otherwise use this naming policy with the zh-CN title as the primary compression/style reference and JP wording as the semantic/reference guard when available.
If zh-CN and JP imply materially different imagery, wordplay, or proper-noun treatment and the conflict cannot be resolved confidently, defer instead of inventing a permanent title.
source_strategy: When zh-CN is available, learn from how it compresses the skill into a short title; do not mechanically translate every character.
Use Japanese wording/aliases to protect the original motif, role/title gimmick, proper noun, pun, and semantic distinction.
Do not use UmaTL English translation text as AI input.
The zh-CN title is a naming/style guide, not authority for character/racehorse proper nouns.
naming_rules: Aim for roughly 2-4 meaningful Vietnamese/Han-Viet units for compact source titles when natural; do not pad the title with explanatory words.
Prefer concise Han-Viet compounds when they are intelligible, evocative, and faithful; use polished Vietnamese when Han-Viet would be stiff or opaque.
Mechanical/common skill families should read like compact ability labels, not prose: action or property + context is usually enough.
Rare, gold, unique, evolution, or stylized names may be more literary, but should still sound like a commercial-game ability name rather than a dictionary gloss.
Preserve a distinctive title/role gimmick when it is part of the identity. Example: 教授 should remain Giáo Sư in 弧线教授 instead of being flattened to Bậc Thầy.
Preserve grade/symbol markers exactly, including ○, ×, ◎, ☆ and runtime/markup tokens.
Do not prepend generic words such as Kỹ năng/Skill to an individual skill name unless the source itself names that category.
Do not rewrite a skill name into a sentence describing its effect. Mechanical precision belongs in the description.
In skill descriptions, keep player-facing gameplay terms such as Speed, Stamina, Power, Guts, Wit, Turf, Dirt, Distance and Style labels according to ui_community_terms.json.
capitalization: Use Vietnamese game-title capitalization for canonical skill titles: capitalize meaningful title words consistently; preserve source symbols.
